title: Lauri Törni — the soldier who fought for three countries
sources: Wikipedia: Lauri Törni (28 May 1919 – 18 October 1965), later Larry Alan Thorne — Finnish-born soldier who fought under three countries: as a Finnish Army officer in the Winter War and Continuation War; as a Waffen-SS officer against the Red Army; and as a US Army Special Forces officer in Vietnam. In the Winter War he fought at Lake Ladoga; in 1943 'Detachment Törni' operated deep behind Soviet lines; the Soviet Army put a bounty of 3,000,000 Finnish marks on his head; Mannerheim Cross, 9 July 1944. After Finland's armistice he joined the Waffen-SS in 1945 to fight Soviet troops near Schwerin, surrendered to the British, escaped a POW camp; in Finland he was convicted of treason in 1947 (six years), escaped prison, was recaptured and pardoned in 1948. In 1949 he went to Sweden, then Venezuela, stowed away on a ship to the US and jumped overboard in the Gulf of Mexico near Mobile, Alabama, and swam ashore. Granted residence by an Act of Congress in 1953; enlisted in the US Army in 1954 as Larry Thorne; joined the Special Forces, taught skiing and survival, served with the 10th Special Forces Group at Bad Tölz, appears in a 1962 'Big Picture' episode filmed in 1959. In Vietnam he won two Purple Hearts and a Bronze Star; on 18 October 1965 his CH-34 helicopter disappeared in bad weather during a covert MACV-SOG mission; his remains were found in 1999 and buried at Arlington in 2003.

Photos (public domain / CC0, Wikimedia Commons / Finnish Wartime Photograph Archive SA-kuva / US Army): Lauri Törni in 1944; Törni in 1951; the last known photo of Törni in Vietnam; Finnish soldiers in 1944; the Battle of Ilomantsi

Archive film (public domain): 'The Big Picture: Special Forces' (US Army, episode filmed with the 10th Special Forces Group); 'Why We Fight: The Battle of Russia' (1943); 'Operation San Angelo' (US Army, Vietnam 1968) — illustrative
Music: Sibelius, Valse triste — Judith Bokor (cello, 78 rpm recording), public domain

post.facebook:
Remember the soldier who fought for three armies — and might be a legend? This one is real.

Lauri Törni fought for Finland, for Nazi Germany, and for the United States. He was 20 when the Soviet Union invaded Finland in 1939. By 1944 his unit was raiding deep behind Soviet lines, and Moscow put a bounty of 3,000,000 Finnish marks on his head.

Then Finland made peace. Törni didn't. In 1945 he joined the German SS to keep fighting the Soviets. He surrendered to the British, escaped their prison camp and went home — where Finland convicted him of treason. He escaped from prison too, was pardoned and left the country. He stowed away on a ship to America, jumped overboard in the Gulf of Mexico and swam ashore.

In 1954 he joined the US Army as "Larry Thorne", became a Green Beret and taught American soldiers to fight in the snow. On 18 October 1965, in Vietnam, his helicopter flew into the clouds on a secret mission and vanished. His remains were found in 1999; he is buried at Arlington.

A hero to some, a traitor to others — and a soldier of three flags. 👇

#History #WW2 #LauriTorni #GreenBeret

youtube.description:
Lauri Törni fought for three countries. A Finnish hero of the Winter and Continuation Wars with a Soviet bounty on his head, he joined the Waffen-SS in 1945 to keep fighting the Soviets, was convicted of treason in Finland, escaped prison, swam ashore in the US and, as "Larry Thorne", became a US Army Green Beret. He disappeared in a helicopter over Vietnam in 1965; his remains were found in 1999 and buried at Arlington.
